name: logo-overwide-banner
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 28 - File > Export > Export As > SVG
story: A designer drew a full-width sponsor banner across the bottom of a 1920x1080 frame - 1600px wide by 100px tall, a 16:1 aspect ratio - filled it with banner artwork and a disclaimer label, and exported from Adobe Illustrator with Styling set to Presentation Attributes and Images set to Embed.
idioms: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> prolog - Illustrator uses lowercase utf-8, not UTF-8
<!-- Generator: Adobe Illustrator 28.3, SVG Export Plug-In ... --> comment on line 2
x="0px" y="0px" on the root <svg> element alongside width and height
xmlns:xlink declared on the root, used for xlink:href on the <image>
a placed raster as a POSITIONED <image> with x/y/width/height and xlink:href="data:image/png;base64,..." - not a <pattern>
font-family as a quoted PostScript name in a presentation attribute: font-family="'Inter-Medium'"
tab indentation throughout, layer id using underscores (Sponsor_banner, Banner_backplate, Banner_art, Disclaimer)
a space in a layer name written as Illustrator's _x20_ escape (id="Banner_x20_backplate", id="Sponsor_x20_banner"), so the label the operator sees is decoded rather than read raw
whyThisMatters: A 16:1 banner is the widest logo shape the corpus has - wider than any wordmark or strap tested before. Illustrator writes a placed image as a positioned <image>, not the Figma <pattern> idiom, so this file also tests the importer's Illustrator image path at an extreme scale. If the width calculation clips or rounds the image field dimensions, the banner artwork will be cropped on-air when an operator swaps the logo into a narrow slot.
